field: report-prose.md:21, first sentence of Short-form pipeline
correct_value: Context papers, experiments under 50 people, designs that the abstract called non-random, and experiments whose abstract did not say how people were assigned went through one screener and citation checking. Of the 186 short forms, 129 have a saved independent checker record; the remaining 57 have no saved checker record and no matching job in the supplied Codex job logs. The checker protocol required finding each cited passage independently and using a fixer when the checker disagreed.
evidence: The assembled report, creativity-screening-2026-10-04.md:21, describes independent checking as completed for the short-form set; report-prose.md:21 contains that wording. Independently enumerating forms/c<digits>.json gives 186 forms whose screener starts with single. Exactly 129 have a matching forms/checks/<cid>.json; all 129 parse and identify the matching cid. The other 57 have no checker file. Parsing every record in the six codex-jobs/jobs-*.jsonl files finds no reference to any of those 57 cids. For example, c027 and c066 have screener=single and no checker file or job. All 186 short forms have citation-check files. tools/codex_pipeline.py:332-348 defines the independent checker and requires its output at forms/checks/<cid>.json; lines 352-361 define the fixer. The records support documented checking for 129 forms, not the blanket completion claim; absence of records does not establish that undocumented checking was impossible.

field: report-prose.md:44, phrase '{{n_small_unreported}} of them report only the number randomized'
correct_value: {{n_small_unreported}} of them have no analyzed participant count recorded
evidence: The assembled report:52 says seven report only the number randomized. report-data.json has 27 small-status papers, 20 entries in small_n, and n_small_without_analyzed_count=7. The seven absent from small_n are c018, c250, c614, c644, c683, c983, and c996; their randomized studies all have participants.n_analyzed=null. Only five have a recorded n_randomized: c250/S1=20, c614/S2=48, c644/S1=27, c683/S2=40, and c983/S1=12. I opened their retrieval.json pdf_path files with PyMuPDF and checked PDF p. 5 Sections 3.1-3.2 (c250), p. 8 Participants/Design study and Table 2 (c614), p. 6 Section 3.4 (c644: randomized teams with 16 and 11 students), p. 9 Section 5.1 (c683: 40 individuals in randomized teams), and p. 10 Sections 5.1-5.2 (c983: 12 students and randomized within-person conditions). forms/c018.json and forms/c996.json have both n_randomized and n_analyzed null. The c018 PDF, pp. 14-15 Appendix A.1, reports 38 recruits, filtering an unspecified number after their first session, and reassignment of sessions; it does not separately resolve the assignment-stage and analyzed-person totals. The c996 PDF, p. 6 Sections 4.1-4.2, reports 20 recruits and one person completing only the no-plugin sprint, without a separate randomized-person total. The report rows at lines 1682 and 1697 accordingly say not reported without a randomized count. tools/build_report.py:189-198 counts missing analyzed counts; tools/assemble_report.py:107 correctly inserts that count. The unsupported interpretation originates in report-prose.md, so the correction renders as seven lacking a recorded analyzed count.
